Definition: from G1909 and G991; to gaze at (with favor, pity or partiality):--look upon, regard, have respect to.
BiblicalUsage: Epiblepo means to look upon with favour, pity, or partiality. Mary sings that God hath regarded the low estate of His handmaiden; a father cries, look upon my son, for he is mine only child; and James warns against looking with respect to the man in fine clothing while the poor man stands.
TheologicalSignificance: God looks on the lowly with favour, and I must not look on the rich with favour. I believe the word convicts me twice, and His gaze and mine should point the same way: toward the low estate, not the fine clothing.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
